Premature Birth Taught Me the Dark Comedy of Trauma

What followed that day is a blurry haze. When I try to remember specifics, it plays in my mind like quick cuts in a television show: A kind resident swabbing my cervix calmly, but then returning to the triage room with a larger group of doctors, all with somber faces. A fast transfer to a labor and delivery room. A steroid shot for my baby’s lungs and a magnesium drip for his brain; IV antibiotics and a fetal monitor. Our son, holding on.
